Civics is the study of the rights and responsibilities of citizens. It refers to anything related to the role of individuals in their community and their country. Being knowledgeable about civics helps people understand how to be active and engaged members of society.

Who is a Citizen?

A citizen is a person who belongs to a country, either by birth or by becoming a citizen through a legal process called naturalization. Citizenship means that a person has both certain rights and responsibilities within that country.

Some people divide a citizen’s role into civic duties and civic responsibilities .

Civic Duties Civic duties American citizens have a duty to obey the laws of their nation and defend the Constitution. For example, they must send their children to school. They must join a military force to defend the country if needed. Citizens must pay their taxes, and they must serve on a jury or as a witness in court if asked.

To be responsible citizens, Americans use their most valuable democratic right: the right to vote. A good citizen will keep herself or himself informed about events and politics, so she or he can vote wisely. Responsible citizens even take part in government if they can. Another responsibility Americans have is to their community and fellow citizens.

Good citizens think about the welfare of others and respect their rights and beliefs.

Civil Rights – The Five Freedoms The constitution has many amendments that tell us our rights and responsibilities as US citizens. The First Amendment to the Constitution gave American citizens five “freedoms,” or civil rights. They are: 1. Freedom of religion : the government cannot create an official religion. Citizens have the freedom to attend the church, synagogue, temple or mosque of their choice – or not attend at all. 2. Freedom of speech : the government cannot create laws to try to stop citizens from expressing rational opinions. Citizens can be critical about the government and share their opinions with others. 3. Freedom of press : the government cannot control what is printed in newspapers, magazines, and books, broadcast on TV or radio, or offered online. 4. Freedom of assembly : citizens can get together with other people in public and private gatherings. They can join groups for political, religious, social or recreational purposes. 5. Freedom to petition the government : citizens can present requests to the government without fear of punishment. They can protest about unfair actions or laws, and they have the right to request change.

Your social studies test may ask questions that show you can identify a principle or apply a principle to a situation. Des Moines Independent Community School District , 393 U.S. 503 (1969) In December of 1965, three students were suspended for wearing black armbands to school to protest the Vietnam War. The school argued the display was a distraction and possibly a danger to students, and the case went all the way up the judicial chain. But in 1969, the Supreme Court, the highest court in the country, decided that the armbands didn’t invade the rights of others. In fact, the school asking students to remove the bands infringed upon their rights. QUESTION : Which one of the five freedoms do you think the Supreme Court was upholding with its decision? (1) Freedom of religion (2) Freedom of speech (3) Freedom of press (4) Freedom of assembly (5) Freedom to petition government The answer is (2) – freedom of speech. The armbands were worn to show opposition to the war in Vietnam, and the Supreme Court decided students’ right to express their opposition was the right to free speech, protected by the First Amendment. The students had this right, even if their school did not like it. This question tests your ability to take ideas and apply them more generally. • Voting : citizens over the age of eighteen have the right to vote. The Fourteenth Amendment guaranteed the right of citizens to be equal, regardless of race.

• Carrying weapons : the Second Amendment grants freedom to bear arms. This means that people can own guns and use a gun in a lawful way. (Most states also require specific permits for various types of guns.)

Today, immigrants are vulnerable to slavery in America. They can be exploited , or taken advantage of, by human traffickers and employers.

Rights of the Accused Several amendments protect the rights of people accused of a crime. Let’s look at what that would mean if you found yourself accused of a crime.

• You have the right to have your case heard by a jury.

• You cannot be tried for the same crime more than once.

• In a court case, the government has to prove your guilt to the jury using evidence . A person is innocent until proven guilty.

• The government cannot force a person to say that they did the crime.

• You are not supposed to wait a long time for a trial to take place.

Any witnesses that are a part of the trial must be brought to the court to testify .

Non-citizens generally have the same constitutional rights as citizens when law enforcement officers stop, question, arrest, or search them or their homes.

Non-citizens have the same right as citizens to remain silent (not answer questions) and ask for a lawyer .

However, the law says adult non-citizens who have immigration documents must carry those documents with them at all times. You should show them to law officers if asked. If you are arrested because you do not have your immigration documents with you, but you have them elsewhere, ask a friend or family member to bring them to you.

In this lesson… You will learn What is the role of a government? What are some different types of government? What is a republican government? What is a democratic government?

Words to know Authoritarian — exercising a lot of control over people

Communism — economic system in which the government controls the economy and there is no private ownership of land, housing, or businesses

Democracy — political system in which the supreme power rests with the wishes of the majority

Economy — anything to do with how people use resources and the flow of money, including housing, jobs, and buying and selling goods and services

Elect — choose a representative by popular vote

Federal — to do with a government of a country that has a central government but also individual states that keep some powers

Inherited — passed on from the previous owner—a person can inherit property or power or other rights

Monarchy — rule by a royal head of state, such as a queen or emperor

Republic — political system in which people elect representatives that make laws and vote on decisions

Society — organized group with shared rules and values

Theocracy — nation where a religion rules in the name of its god

Totalitarian — extremely authoritarian system in which citizens don’t get to vote in free elections or have a say in making laws

The First Governments Ever since people started living in societies, they needed some form of government to make their community function and to help it survive. They made decisions as a group, maybe by voting. They elected leaders to make decisions. For example, An old print shows Native Americans in a government meeting. The Iroquois Nation, in what is now New York State, had a federal system. This meant that separate tribes within the nation governed themselves, but representatives from the tribes met to decide issues that affected the whole nation. Different types of government The role of government is still the same as it was years ago. Over time, different types of government have emerged. Some serve their people, while others control them. Here are some different types of government: Monarchy A monarchy is a nation ruled by a royal, such as a queen or an emperor. Monarchs inherit their power, usually from a member of the same family. Monarchs used to have absolute (total) control. The Queen opens Parliament in an ancient British ceremony. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is a constitutional monarchy AND a parliamentary democracy! A handful of absolute monarchies, such as the country of Oman, still exist today. But most countries that still have monarchs give the governing powers to elected leaders. For example, the British Queen has no real power. Theocracy Another old form of government is a theocracy, a nation where a religion rules in the name of its god. The nation’s laws are based on interpretations of the religion. Examples of theocracies today are Iran and the Vatican City. Authoritarian governments Monarchies and theocracies are dying out, but governments that want to control their citizens still exist. This type of government is an authoritarian government. Authoritarian governments can have many different kinds of political and economic systems. What they share is how much control they have over their citizens. For example, North Korea is a totalitarian state. There is no choice of leader and the state has extreme control over society through its military forces. It also has a communist economy. Dictatorships Extreme authoritarian governments are called totalitarian governments, or dictatorships. Citizens don’t have any say about leaders or laws. They may be punished or killed for opposing the government. North Korea is a country run by a totalitarian government. Authoritarian governments often don’t hold free and fair elections. And if they do, they may offer only one option – the ruling dictator – so it isn’t really a free election anyway. Communist nations Communist countries usually have authoritarian governments. In a communist economic system, the government controls the economy and there is no private ownership of land, housing, or businesses. One of communism’s goals is to create a society where everyone is equal or a classless society.

GED Exam Tip

Exam tip Many questions in your social studies test will test how well you analyze text. Some text is just information, while other text offers points of view, opinions, and conclusions. A conclusion is the belief a person ends up with after thinking about something. Your analysis of conclusions shows that you can tell the difference between facts and opinions and recognize connections between statements. Here is a short, opinionated essay about communism that ends with a conclusion: WHY COMMUNISM DOES NOT WORK Communism is a system of government that claims to make everyone equal and to give power to the workers. In the early 1800s, the German philosopher Karl Marx said that it is unfair for some people to be rich and for others to be poor. He said that the only solution to this inequality was to get rid of private ownership of property. Under communism, everyone would own everything together. But when communism was put into practice in Communist Russia, people had very little freedom. Russian citizens also became very poor under communist rule. People were forced to do the work that the government dictated, and violence against Russian citizens became common. It is easy to convince poor people that communism works. But do not believe people who tell you communism is better than capitalism! A life under communism means a life without choices. Answer this question: Which fact supports the author’s conclusion that “A life under communism means a life without choices”? A. It is unfair for some people to be rich and for others to be poor. B. Russian citizens became very poor under communist rule. C. People were forced to do the work that the government dictated, and violence against Russian citizens became common. D. Communism is the easiest system to sell to people who are poor. In one of our history lessons, you learned how to tell facts from opinions. This question asked us for a supporting fact, so let’s eliminate the opinions in the statements first. Both A and D sound like opinions, because other people could agree or disagree with them. B and C seem more like facts because they could be proven to be true by checking with other sources. So let’s look at those two statements and test them to find the best choice. Statement B says Russians became very poor, but being poor is not the same as having no choices, so this does not support the author’s conclusion. C says that people were forced to do certain work. Being forced to do something means you have no choice, so statement C supports the author’s conclusion. When a question asks you to find evidence or supporting statements, remember to use your earlier tips for testing statements and telling facts from opinions.

Government in the United States The United States is a form of republic called a federal republic .

In a federal republic , a lot of government decisions take place at State level. In the USA, for example, some decisions about health care and education vary from state to state, and others are the same for the whole nation.

Republics In a republic, the people elect representatives who make laws and vote on decisions. Some republics are authoritarian, but most make laws and run the country according to the wishes of citizens. Democracy In a democracy, the supreme power rests with the wishes of the majority of its citizens. Another important aspect of democracy is that people are free to disagree with the government. The United States is a presidential democracy because it has a president with certain powers. A common feature of democratic countries is that they have multiple political parties. These parties are groups of people with differing political beliefs. They can be in the government together because in a democracy, people are free to hold different opinions. You will learn about political parties in the next lesson.

Economy — anything to do with how people use resources and the flow of money, including housing, jobs, and buying and selling goods and services

The United States of America is also a presidential democracy. In a democracy, the supreme power rests with the wishes of the majority, and people are free to disagree with the government.

In this lesson… You will learn What are the two main political parties in America? What do Democrats believe? What do Republicans believe? What is public policy?

Words to know Conservative — supporting traditional ideas

Debate — discuss or argue about something

Lobbyist — person who persuades politicians to pass laws that are good for the group they represent, which could be anything from an industry to an environmental organization

Policy — a set of beliefs or plan for the way something should be done

Political platform — official beliefs and goals of a political party or candidate

Progressive — supporting new ideas

Special Interest Groups — organization that pressures government officials to support or change laws that are favorable to its causes

Regulate — control how things are done

Welfare programs — government support given to help people in need

Political Parties Political parties are groups made up of regular citizens and politicians. They come together to support certain goals and policies. Policies are plans or ideas for how the government should work and how problems should be solved.

In the United States, power has shifted between different political parties over time. Today, there are two main political parties:

• Democrats

• Republicans

There are also some smaller political parties, but Democrats and Republicans are the largest and most well-known.

Each political party has a set of ideas, called a political platform . This platform is the foundation for what the party stands for and what they want to achieve. Not everyone in the party agrees on every issue, but in general, Democrats and Republicans have different beliefs about how the government should run and solve problems.

The Republican Platform Republicans use an elephant as a symbol for their party. Sometimes they are called the “GOP,” which stands for Grand Old Party . They are also known as conservatives , the “right,” or “right-wing.”

• Republicans believe laws and rules for business and economics should be as few as possible.

• Republicans do not support many public welfare programs .

• Republicans believe in high military spending and strong military forces.

• Republicans are socially conservative and want to retain respect for traditional values and ideas about society.

• Many Republicans oppose abortion.

• Many Republicans oppose gay marriage.

• Republicans think that taxes should be as low as possible and that government spending should be reduced.

• Republicans generally believe that environmental regulations hurt business.

• Republicans support the right to own guns.

• Most Republicans are less favorable to immigration than most Democrats.

The Democratic Platform

Democrats have a donkey as the symbol of their party. Democrats and other progressive groups are also called the “left” or “left-wing.”

• Democrats believe in regulating business and the environment.

• Many Democrats believe American military spending is too high.

• Many Democrats are socially progressive, which means they support new ideas. This is the opposite of conservative. Democrats want society’s values to respect differences and freedom of choice.

• Democrats support a woman’s right to decide whether or not to end her pregnancy.

• Democrats support gay marriage.

• Democrats generally support higher taxes to fund social programs (welfare) that help low-income citizens.

• Democrats are in favor of regulations that protect the environment.

• Democrats believe gun ownership should be strictly regulated.

• Most Democrats are more favorable to immigration than most Republicans.

It is good to remember that not all Republicans and Democrats support everything in their parties’ platforms.

Small Political Parties In addition to the two main political parties, there are a few smaller political parties in the U.S. These smaller parties don’t have as much influence but still have important ideas.

Logo of Libertarian Party

Libertarians believe the government should stay out of people's lives as much as possible. They want low taxes and limited government spending, similar to the Republicans. However, like the Democrats, they also believe in personal freedoms, meaning people should have the right to make their own choices in life.

Logo of Green Party

The Green Party focuses on protecting the environment. They support policies that promote clean energy and saving natural resources. The Green Party believes the government should play a strong role in protecting the planet through rules and regulations.

What is Public Policy? The term “public policy” refers to a set of actions the government takes to address issues within society. For example, public policy addresses problems over the long-term, such as issues with healthcare or gun control.

Different parties have different policies. Public policy is a government’s plan for putting their platform into action. In a good government, these policies also respond to the needs or changing beliefs of a nation. America has policies about immigration, crime, and foreign affairs. These policies affect the laws politicians make.

Some public policies are debated , which means discussed or argued about, because of the problems they cause . Others are debated because people disagree on what actions will solve problems.

For example, Democrats and Republicans argue about how healthcare should be provided and paid for. Healthcare in America is a large part of the economy – almost 20 percent of it! It costs the government and citizens a huge amount of money every year.

On your test, you will probably be asked to interpret and identify points made in political cartoons. These are cartoons published in newspapers throughout American history, making jokes or comments about political issues of the time. Political cartoons try to make people think about serious issues or even affect their opinions. Questions about political cartoons will not test your knowledge. They will test your critical thinking skills: your ability to make inferences and recognize a point of view. (An inference is a conclusion you reach or judgment you make from looking at or reading something.) Let’s use this knowledge about points of view to answer a question about a cartoon. You are going to infer what point of view the cartoon below is expressing. Here is some background information to the cartoon: Politicians argue about the best policy for providing healthcare to Americans. In 2010, the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act was signed. It is often called “Obamacare” because it was the plan of President Barack Obama, shown here leading a giant “Obamacare” baby by the hand. The other figure in the cartoon is Uncle Sam, who represents the USA. The law says everyone must have health insurance to cover their medical expenses. People argued about the new law. A lot of people said it took away their freedom of choice and cost too much. Others argued it would cost less money in the long run and helped poor people afford health insurance. The cartoon was published in 2013. Question: What opinion is being expressed in the political cartoon? A. Obamacare will grow to be too big and expensive. B. Obamacare is something to celebrate. C. Barack Obama is the leading politician supporting Obamacare. D. Obamacare is three years old. B must be incorrect, because Uncle Sam is worried about costs. C and D are true, but they are not opinions and they are not the main point of the cartoon. Answer A is the best answer because it expresses a point of view and is the main idea of the cartoon.

Debate — discuss or argue about something

Lobbyist — person who persuades politicians to pass laws that are good for the group they represent, which could anything from an industry to an environmental organization

Policy — a set of beliefs or plan for the way something should be done

Political platform — official beliefs and goals of a political party or candidate

Progressive — supporting new ideas

Special Interest Groups — organization that pressures government officials to support or change laws that are favorable to its causes

Welfare programs — government support given to help people in need

In this lesson… You will learn What was the Scientific Revolution? What was the Industrial Revolution? How did the Industrial Revolution change society? What is the economy? How did the modern economy develop? What is supply and demand?

Words to know Assembly Line — process in a factory where each person makes one part of a product and then passes it on to the next person. The product passes from one worker to another until it is finished.

Economics — study of how people use resources

Economy — flow of goods, services, and money

Goods — things that are bought and sold

Industrial — to do with factories and machinery used to make things

Rational — based on facts and logic instead of beliefs

Textiles — woven or knitted cloth

The Scientific Revolution A revolution is a complete change in how a society is organized. The Scientific Revolution and the Industrial Revolution are different from other revolutions in history. They were not wars or uprisings. Instead, they brought about revolutions, or big changes, in the way people did things.

Artist's impression of Nicholas Copernicus. Courtesy: aish.com

The Scientific Revolution was a long period of great discoveries. It began in the mid-1500s and continued to about 1800. It was a time when people began to use scientific observation and rational thought to understand more about the world.

Until the Scientific Revolution, most people believed that Earth was at the center of the universe and that the Sun and other planets traveled around it. But in 1543, the astronomer Nicholas Copernicus said that Earth and other planets revolved around the Sun. When telescopes were invented in the early 1600s, his theory was proved right. Scientific ideas slowly began to spread.

Inventions such as the telescope and the microscope helped advance the Scientific Revolution. The telescope increased people’s understanding of the universe. The microscope advanced medical knowledge because scientists were able to see tiny cells and other things too small for the human eye to see. They learned more about how living things worked, and that helped them figure out how to cure diseases.

The Industrial Revolution The Industrial Revolution began in the 1770s and lasted until the early 1900s. Before this time, most jobs were done by hand, and people traveled by walking or using animals. Farmers used animals and simple tools to work the land.

The invention of the steam engine changed everything. In the 1700s, steam engines became powerful enough to run machines and pull trains. This meant people didn’t have to make things by hand anymore—machines could do it for them. Machines also transformed farming because one machine could do the work of several workers.

In the late 1800s, electricity was discovered and used to power even more machines, bringing big changes to everyday life.

In 1913, the Ford Motor Company became the first company to use the moving assembly line in its factories. This invention meant that workers could make cars in much less time. It cut the cost and soon, many Americans wanted to buy cars. Image courtesy of Ford Motor Company Media Center

In 1913 , the Ford Motor Company was the first to use the moving assembly line in its factories. This new method allowed cars to be made much faster, reducing the cost. As a result, many Americans wanted to buy cars.

As machines became more common, people moved from farms to cities to work in factories that made textiles, metal tools, and engine parts. By 1850 , large cities had grown, and railroads connected people and places like never before. By the 1900s , the Industrial Revolution had spread worldwide. In the 20th century, inventions like the assembly line and the airplane continued to change how people lived and worked.

GED Exam Tip Exam tip In your social studies test, math test, and science test, you will probably get questions about a table of information. A table is a neat way of presenting information such as dates and categories or short descriptions. Below is a typical table. Some tables look more complicated than this one and may involve more numbers. But in your test, all the information you need will be in the table and any text that comes with it. When you see a table in the test, be prepared to do some careful reading and simple calculations (sums), and to use some basic knowledge and reasoning skills. You may also be asked to make predictions (guess what happens next). Whether the table appears in social studies, math, or science tests, you’ll probably be asked to choose a true or false statement. Let’s try a question based on this table. The table above shows some important inventions of the Industrial Revolution. QUESTION: Using the information in the table, choose the false statement below. A. More than 100 years after James Watts invented the steam engine, two other important devices used for motion were invented. B. Diesel fuel, Ford motor cars, and Morse telegraph code were all named for their inventors. C. Isaac Singer made improvements to Howe’s sewing machine 27 years after it was invented. D. Two huge advances in transportation took place in the 20th century. E. Three 19th-century inventions improved communications. As with all true and false questions,

you will quickly check the answers against the information given – in this case, a table. Let’s run through the statements: A. Motors and engines are both devices used for motion. According to the table, the steam engine was invented in 1775, and the electric motor and diesel engine were invented in 1888 and 1892, both more than 100 years later, so this statement is true. B. A quick look at the table, which lists inventors’ names as well as their inventions, shows this statement is very likely to be true. Inventors named Diesel, Morse, and Ford all have inventions on the table. You can infer (draw conclusions) from the type of inventions that the fuel, the code, and the car were all named for them because of what they invented. C. A quick calculation shows that 7 years passed between Howe’s sewing machine and Singer’s sewing machine, not 27 years. So this statement is false, and this is the answer you will choose. D. The invention of both the airplane and the assembly line created huge changes in transportation, and they both happened in the 20th century, so this statement is true. The basic knowledge you need is that the 19th century means dates beginning 1801 to 1900, and the 20th century means dates from 1901 to 2000. E. The telegraph, the cable, and the telephone are all for communication, and they were all invented in the 19th century, so this statement is true.

Economy and Revolutions Courtesy: geographicbook.com

The economy is the way goods, services, and money are exchanged in a country or around the world. Before the Industrial and Scientific Revolutions, most economies were based on farming. People grew crops and raised animals to make a living.

Then, scientific discoveries led to the rise of industry . Industry created machines that could do farming work and factories that could produce large amounts of goods. This caused the economy to grow and change as new products and opportunities became available.

Today, some people believe we are going through another major change, called the Technological Revolution . This change is being driven by computers and the internet . Computers are now doing many jobs that people used to do, just like machines took over farming jobs in the past. Because of this, the economy is changing once again.

Supply and Demand One economic idea you may see in your test is the concept of supply and demand . Supply means the amount of a product that is offered. Demand means how much people want. The economy (and the price) depends on a balance between the two.

The Industrial Revolution was a change in the way people made things. The Industrial Revolution used the new knowledge to develop machines and new forms of power, such as steam engines and electricity, that did the work instead of humans and animals. The Industrial Revolution led to mass manufacturing in factories, new forms of transportation and communication, and the growth of cities. The economy means the exchange of goods, services, and money. The economy has changed and continues to change with new developments, first in industry and later in technology. The economy depends on a balance between supply and demand.

In this lesson… You will learn Why do we pay taxes? What are taxes for? Who must pay taxes? What are the different kinds of taxes that Americans pay? Where does most tax money get spent?

Words to know Income — money a person or business earns or receives

Infrastructure — government and school buildings, roads, bridges, railways, power plants, and communications systems in a nation or community

Revenue — income received by a government or a business

Social security — government program that collects money from workers and businesses to provide income to people when they get old or sick

Tax — amount of money people must pay to the government

Tax return — document people and businesses submit to the government to declare their income and expenses

A tax is an amount of money people must pay to the government. It is usually a percentage of some other amount, but sometimes it is a flat fee. We pay taxes to cover the costs of running a country, state, town, or public program. By paying taxes, citizens contribute to the government programs that benefit them and their communities. This means everything from the huge costs of the US military or welfare programs to the local library or park in your neighborhood. Taxes Americans pay go to the federal government, state governments, and the smaller, local governments that run counties and cities. If you earn money spend money, or own property, you will pay tax of one kind or another. Let’s learn about the different types of tax people and businesses pay. Income tax Income tax is a tax on what you earn, or your income. People pay income tax to the federal government and to most state governments. Some states, such as New Hampshire and Florida, do not charge income tax. The rate, or amount, of taxes, depends on how much you earn and what your expenses are. People who earn more money pay a higher percentage of their incomes in taxes than people who have less money. This is known as a progressive tax. Every year, workers and businesses have to figure out, or calculate, their income and certain expenses. Then they calculate how much tax they owe and send their figures to the government. This process is called filing a tax return. Many employees have tax deducted from their paychecks before they receive their pay. If you pay these deductions, your tax return at the end of the year may show you’ve already paid too much tax, and the government owes you. Income tax goes to the US government’s Treasury, which is the national finance department. Some of the money collected by the Treasury then funds states and their schools, hospitals, and roads. States get the rest of their income from various other taxes. These could be a state income tax or a state sales tax. Some states have both. Two states, Alaska and New Hampshire, have neither. Learn more about your taxes as a US Citizen ■ Check for understanding What do income taxes pay for? Sales tax and property tax A sales tax is a tax you pay when you buy something or pay for a service. If you buy a new

book, you may have to pay a small percentage on top of the price. That money goes to the state. In most states, there is no tax on food or medicine. Not all states have sales tax, including Alaska, New Hampshire, and Oregon. Every state government decides what additional local taxes are charged. They might let towns and counties collect extra sales taxes, or allow taxes on services such as telephone and electricity. A lodging tax is a tax on hotel rooms. Cities or regions that have a lot of tourists make a lot of income from this kind of tax. Most local government revenue, however, comes from property tax. A property tax is an annual amount charged on any building or land. The higher the value of the property, the more money you pay every year. It is a tax on what you own. Example of state and local tax distribution for Ohio in 2007. Government spending The amount that governments spend usually changes every year. In 2014, the US federal government spent around 3.5 trillion dollars. The money went toward programs such as social security , which pays monthly income to retired and disabled people. A lot of money goes toward health care. It also goes toward funding the government and military, paying for public schools, and paying for infrastructure , such as bridges and roads.

GED Exam Tip Exam tip Some questions on your social studies test simply require you to think clearly. Once again, these questions are not testing your knowledge. They are asking you to use your reasoning skills. You will want to read carefully and make sure you understand the topic and the question. This question is about tax revenue. It is also about cause and effect – what makes something happen and what the result is. You are going to use your reasoning skills to choose the best answer. Here is the background text: In 2007, the Iowa state government passed a law allowing counties in Iowa to impose an extra one-cent sales tax on clothes and footwear to raise more revenue. But raising sales tax actually reduced revenue for some counties in 2008. QUESTION : Why could this have happened? Select all the reasons below that may have caused a reduction in revenue for some counties. A. People went to a neighboring county to buy their clothes and footwear so they could avoid paying the tax. B. When sales tax went up, people had to get another job to pay it. C. The price increased, and so people bought fewer clothes and shoes overall. D. When the county’s revenue from sales tax increased, it received less money from the federal government. E. To avoid sales tax, people started buying clothes and footwear online instead of locally. As you look through these answers, you don’t know for sure that any of these actually happened. But the question was not, What caused this reduction? It was, Why could this have happened? The question is asking you to use your thinking skills to choose possible causes. The best answer to this question is that all of the reasons except Reason B could have caused a reduction in revenue. Reason B would not have reduced revenue. It’s possible that people who wanted to buy lots of clothes would have to get another job to afford them, but it would not have caused a reduction in revenue. If anything, it would cause an increase in revenue as they paid more income tax as well as buying more clothes and shoes! You can see it is not hard to use your reasoning skills. If you stay calm and trust your own common sense, you can figure out the best answer.
